summary: KEEP. Acceptance ① (runtime owns resolution without depending on src-tauri): HelperBinaryResolver lives in r-code-runtime with zero src-tauri dependencies — explicit absolute directory first, else verified siblings of the daemon, never PATH, tampered/missing/unbound refusals, and a digest helper for byte-pinning; the profile carries the binding and the daemon accepts --helper-dir with no daemon-code change. Acceptance ② (both real packaging flows ship helpers): the Windows installer and the macOS script build and stage both helpers with target-triple names beside the daemon, build.rs validates them (and still launches nothing), and both tauri configs declare the identical externalBin set — pinned by a packaging test that fails on any divergence. Acceptance ③ (Tauri and standalone reject missing/tampered helpers): the resolver refuses truncated, garbage-magic and missing helpers as Tampered/Missing (SafeDisabled-shaped refusals, never a PATH fallback), the standalone daemon smoke proves --helper-dir end to end through the real client, and the never-PATH property is proven structurally. Honest disclosures: a dev-mode host check lets tauri-build overwrite real helper artifacts in target/debug with placeholders (packaging mode is unaffected; the QA suite self-heals and the behaviour is recorded); the guardian's real launch session is Linux-native CI territory (s08), with the non-Linux empty-main exit 0 as this host's launch proof; full signature/owner pinning remains P32's release gate with the digest seam in place. House 1081/1080/1 with only the declared plan_schema baseline; the s07 load-race member appeared in two full runs and was green 10/10 in isolation both times, both numbers reported.
